newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota weather favorable for crops, planting.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota weather favorable for crops, planting.

text.p: Improved weather allowed South Dakota farmers to make good planting progress in the week ended Sunday, the state Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop progress report.
There were four days suitable for fieldwork in the week, and warmer temperatures aided emergence and development of seeded crops, said.
Spring wheat was 92 percent emerged, versus 91 percent last year and the five-year average of 96. The crop was rated 78 percent good to excellent, 22 fair and one percent poor.
Winter wheat was rated 45 percent good to excellent, 36 pct fair, and 19 percent poor to very poor.
Winter wheat booted 51 pct vs 35 w/a, 35 y/a, 53 avge.
Winter wheat headed 11 pct vs nil w/a, 3 y/a, 42 avge.
Barley was rated 70 percent good to excellent, 29 fair and two percent poor to very poor.
Corn seeded 94 pct vs 88 week ago, 86 year ago, 85 avge.
Sorghum seeded 41 pct vs 30 w/a, 35 y/a, 53 avge.
Topsoil moisture was rated 24 percent surplus, 63 percent adequate, 12 percent short and one percent very short.
